question: does the mid confidence band also need modal recomputation, and what does confidence actually predict
design: ten mid-band items sampled with a fixed seed, five repeats each, same judge and artifacts; compared with the low and high band results measured in the previous cycle
finding: within-item stability is similar in the mid and low bands, 0.86 against 0.88, but the recorded single draw is representative of the item modal answer in 9 of 10 mid-band cases and only 1 of 5 low-band cases. Reported confidence predicts whether a draw represents the item, not how concentrated the item answer distribution is.
consequence: the modal recomputation rule stays scoped to verdicts below 0.7 confidence, which is now supported by measurement on the mid band rather than assumed

counterevidence_recorded.claim: majority vote can reduce per-problem accuracy on hard problems, and agreement can be high while the answer is wrong
counterevidence_recorded.why_it_matters_here: the modal rule was applied precisely to the hardest items, so aggregation could entrench a wrong answer rather than recover a right one; the human calibration labels are the only arbiter of that risk and none exist yet
counterevidence_recorded.action: the risk is recorded against RD-2026-09-02-31A rather than resolved

limits: ten mid-band items and five low-band items are small samples
no human label exists for any item, so representativeness is not correctness
